limitations: This is one production band-shard observation on c6i.4xlarge. Exporting was 1354.2 s, 26.5% below r5 and 1.3% below the older 1372.2 s single-load baseline; it supports recovery to baseline-like speed, not a general throughput acceleration claim.

The run retained r5 read geometry and count: 25424 rio_read calls, 12.649 per intersecting item. Mean receive throughput was 9.065 MB/s over 12266.6 MB, and mean CPU was 2.74 busy cores (17.1% of 16 vCPU). There is no claim of a read-throughput fix; the gain is removing repeated setup while bounding memory.
Peak RSS was 14807.8 MiB (14.46 GiB), below the 28672 MiB gate. The heartbeat series repeatedly returned to roughly 3.2-5.9 GiB between group waves, consistent with previous groups being released.

Both full production pixel arrays exactly match r5: zero differing pixels and max_abs_diff 0 for lst_p95 and qa_count. Longitude pixel scale metadata differs by 3.8e-19 degrees, about 6.8e-15 degrees over the full width; all other compared metadata matches. The operator explicitly approved passing under the pre-registered shape/dtype/pixel criterion with this limitation retained.

The instance ran on-demand despite requested spot policy. 6.6312 credits are the direct Coiled billing debit. $0.288756 is derived from the 1528.709 s cluster lifecycle at a $0.68/hour c6i.4xlarge on-demand rate and is not an AWS invoice.

An initial proposed r6 prefix received copied plan/items but no cloud launch after the submitter refused to overwrite an existing v2 offset record. The only cluster launched was r6b, cluster 2002585, one attempt with retries disabled.
